bodyHtml:
Modifier Catchall term for something that affects the roll.

EG: Bonus, Malus, Dice Bonus, Dice Malus
Bonus A +[x] modifier to the roll.

EG: +1 Bonus will modify a 2d6k1 skill roll to 2d6k1+1 Abbreviated to B
Dice Bonus A +[x] dice modifier to the roll

EG: +1 Dice Bonus will modify a 2d6k1 skill roll to 3d6k1 Abbreviated to DB
Malus A -[x] modifier to the roll
EG: -1 Malus will modify a 2d6k1 skill roll to 2d6k1-1 Abbreviated to M
Dice Malus A -[x] dice modifier to the roll

EG: -1 Dice Malus will modify a 2d6k1 skill roll to 1d6

Abbreviated to DM

bodyHtml:
Game Master The star of the show, equivalent to a Dungeon master.

Abbreviated to GM.
Player A player controlling a character.
Character Someone within the world, they are assigned stats just like anyone else, and can either be controlled by the Game Master or a Player. Doesn't necessarily have to be a ‘Human’.

GMPC is the term for characters controlled by Game Masters.

PC is the term for characters controlled by Players
Margin of Success (MOS) A character's degree of success in a test. In action tests, if a character meets or surpasses a threshold, the margin of success is their result minus the threshold. In opposed action tests, it's their result minus their opponent's result.
EG: a result of 5 against a threshold of 2 is an MOS of 3 (5 − 2 = 3).
Margin of Failure (MOF) A character's degree of failure in a test. In action tests, if a character fails to meet a threshold, the margin of failure is the threshold minus their result. In opposed action tests, it's their opponent's result minus their own.
EG: a result of 4 against a threshold of 6 is an MOF of 2 (6 − 4 = 2).
Consume/Spend Use a specific resource, such as E-Dice, ammo, grenades, or gadget charges.

EG: Consuming 1 E-dice reduces the total amount of E-dice you have stocked by 1.
Ignore Negate or don’t account for a condition, mechanic, or affliction during tests, under some conditions.
Restore/Restock Restore a specific resource, such as E-Dice, ammo,Grenades, or gadget charges

EG: Restoring all your gadget and ammo charges from an ammo bag will return all of your ammo and gadget charges up to your max capacity.
Attacker A character prompting an opposed action test against another.
Defender A character responding to an opposed action test against another.
Target A character specified as the defender of an opposed action test. Used in the context of afflictions and effects.
Friendly A character that is a member, or allied with your party
Hostile/Contact A character that is not a part of, or against your party.
Wound Overflow Wound Overflow prevents instant death. When a character takes an instance of damage that beats their instant death threshold, and is either from a source with this tag or does an action that causes damage taken to be wound overflow, take a deep wound and subtract the deep wound threshold from the total damage. Repeat this as long as the remaining damage still meets that threshold. Once it doesn’t, repeat this against the flesh wound threshold and take flesh wounds until the remaining damage passes neither threshold.
Temporary Wounds Temporary Wounds are wounds that are gained via CQC attacks and actions during Close Combat. These wounds can be removed by using a [Recover] action, or go away once you exit combat.
Multi Action Penalty (MAP) Occurs when a character initiates a test from both their bonus and standard actions in the same turn, whichever action is taken second incurs a -1 malus to all rolls related to it. This malus applies and is only caused from tests the character chooses to make. It does not apply to tests forced by an external source (e.g. Suppression) or opposed checks made as the defender.
Combat Batch A group of characters in the initiative queue from the same faction or party.

bodyHtml:
Close Range (C) Anything within 8 hexes of a character.
Medium Range (M) Anything within 16 hexes of a character.
Long Range (L) Anything within 24 hexes of a character.
Extreme Long Range (ELR) Anything past 24 hexes of a character but within the map.
Extreme**, Extreme Long Range (EELR)** Anything outside of the boundary of a map, or in other world hexes.
World Hex Specific to Grand Operations

A unit of measurement on the Operations Map equivalent to EELR.

bodyHtml:
Datalink Requires a datalink connection to function. Can be jammed to certain degrees, which causes specific effects.
Airborne Specifies a drone’s domain. When at High Altitude, they are able to have elevation overmatch on all targets in an area and ignore terrain, but cannot enter buildings. When at Low Alt they are able to enter into buildings and smaller spaces, but also have to abide by terrain rules.
Ground Specifies a drone’s domain. They abide by normal movement rules and are affected by cover and elevation.
Breach Can be used to open fences, doors, or walls.
Loitering Lingers or remains in an area for a certain amount of time.
Trap Designates a gadget as being used as a trap. The attacker makes a disguise test when deploying it. Whenever a defender is near the gadget or would otherwise trigger it- they make an alertness test against the threshold set by the attacker’s disguise test. As a bonus action (Eyes Up) characters can scan an area ahead for traps using their Notice skill However- this only checks for traps within close range.
EMP Can disable electronics and gadgets.
Electric Deals electric damage, can cause targets to be tased
Explosive Deals explosive damage, destroys cover and the environment.
Kinetic Deals kinetic damage
Incendiary Deals incendiary damage, can set targets aflame
Vision Affects a character’s ability to see.
NVG Uses night vision, is able to negate lighting conditions.
IR Uses infrared vision, is able to negate weather and lighting conditions
Magnetics Uses magnetic vision, is able to negate weather, lighting conditions, and see through the first wall or cover within line of sight up to medium range (includes through smoke)
Full-Exo Has leg and arm limbs. If the suit limbs are targeted directly (limb sized), each leg damaged will [Cripple] the user, If both legs are damaged, the user is [Debilitated]. Each arm damaged will incur a -1 malus to all action tests. Can be repaired by a technical engineer. Targeting Exosuit limbs does not inflict wounds onto the user.
Half-Exo Has only leg limbs. If the suit limbs are targeted directly (limb sized), each leg damaged will [Cripple] the user, If both legs are damaged, the user is [Debilitated]. Can be repaired by a technical engineer. Targeting Exosuit limbs does not inflict wounds onto the user.
Obscure Obscures vision within or beyond an area.
Repairable Can be repaired using a technical engineer’s repair tool and a repair bonus action.
Resupply Restores ammo, grenades, or gadget charges. Or all three at the same time.
Intercept Intercepts munitions or drones
Ping Applies Pinged to targets.
Mark Applies Marked to targets
Stun Applies Concussed to targets
Interrupt Interrupts an target’s readied action, or ongoing action in some way.
Traversal Can be used to move across a map or area.
-[x] Traceability Applies a -[x] malus to the tech roll due to the traceability of the hack.
Deploy Requires a [Deploy] bonus action to use
Throw Requires a [Throw] full action to use
Shoot Requires a [Shoot] full action to use
CQC Oriented towards closer engagements
Precise Oriented towards longer range engagements
Light Weapons/ L-Wep Uses a Light Weapons skill test.
Medium Weapons/ M-Wep Uses a Medium Weapons skill test.
Heavy Weapons/ H-Wep Uses a Heavy Weapons skill test.
Spray Can use [Spray] when shooting
Burst Can use [Burst] when shooting
Suppression Can use [Suppression] when shooting
Medical Uses a Medical skill test
Stimulant Heals the target
Booster Boosts the capabilities of the target.
Disguise Uses or assists in Disguise skill tests
Stealth Uses or assists in Stealth skill tests

bodyHtml:
Pinged Applies +1 bonus to offensive shooting or throwing actions targeting this character.
Marked Applies +2 bonus to offensive shooting or throwing actions targeting this character.
Suppressed When suppressed, any character not in cover from the source of suppression is immediately knocked prone. At the start of their turn, they must pass a Spirit test against a threshold of 4 or take a -1 dice malus to all rolls and lose the ability to move or make offensive actions for the turn. If the character makes an offensive action, they roll armor against the saturation fire threshold for damage. Removed when the character leaves the line of fire from the source of suppression.
Aflame When aflame, at the end of a character's turn, the character will roll their armor against the burn threshold, which is 3+ the the result of the initial roll that caused the effect, and resolve the damage with Wound Overflow. Removed when the character uses [Patch Up] or someone else does on them. Ignore 2 stage armor systems.
Tased When tased, at the start of a character's turn, they must make a Body test against a threshold of 4. Upon failure, if a weapon is in hand, they immediately fire uncontrollably towards the closest character to them, which counts as their full action for the turn. If no weapon is in hand, they lose their full action instead.
Bleeding When bleeding, at the start of a character’s turn, they take one flesh wound. Removed when the character uses [Patch Up] or someone else does on them.
Winded Applies -1 malus to the character’s next action.
Concussed Applies -1 malus to all of the character’s actions for the turn.
Exhausted Reduces all skills in a category (Alertness, Body, Intelligence, Spirit) to 1 for a specific amount of time
Diminished Reduces all skills in a category (Alertness, Body, Intelligence, Spirit) to 0 for a specific amount of time
Crippled Reduces the total amount of range bands a character can move by 1.
Debilitated Removes a character’s ability to move. Applies -1 to all movement related tests.
Severed Disables a character’s ability to use Datalink enabled equipment, call reinforcements, or use their radio.
Disabled Renders a piece of equipment temporarily inoperable.
Burned Renders a piece of equipment permanently inoperable.
Down But Not Out (DBNO) When wounds surpass your System Shock threshold, or an instance of damage beats a character’s instant death threshold (and they don't use an E-dice) they enter a Down But Not Out state. At the start of each turn they must make a Body test with a threshold of 4. Failing the body test 3 times causes them to become Incapacitated.
Incapacitated When incapacitated, a character is hanging onto life by a thread. They are close to death, and cannot make any actions. They are functionally out of the fight.
